subject: PRECISIONS (NCT04300920)
detail: Genotype-stratified phase 3 of N-acetylcysteine in TOLLIP rs3750920 TT patients; primary completion 2026-03-02, no results posted at 2026-09-03. Request or await results; this is the direct test of the record's only surviving subgroup hypothesis.

subject: closed-access key results
detail: Full text of PMID 26331942 (TOLLIP x N-acetylcysteine interaction) and of the Kangxian Huanji granule trial (PMID 37993378) could not be obtained. Both are marked verification-incomplete and neither can be promoted until read.
phase6_detail: PMID 26331942: the PubMed Central deposit was retrieved but holds front matter and abstract only (closed access, no body). The record's quoted interaction P=0.001 and hazard ratios 0.14 (0.02-0.83) and 3.23 (0.79-13.16) are confirmed against the primary abstract; genotype subgroup sizes, prespecification and the replication cohort remain unverified (correction C37). PMID 37993378 (Kangxian Huanji Granule): no open-access or PubMed Central copy exists, but the full structured abstract was retrieved, establishing a randomised double-blind placebo-controlled design in 80 patients with co-primary endpoints and all secondary effect estimates (correction C36). Smallest next step for both: institutional or publisher access, or an author request; for the granule trial also the ChiCTR1900026289 registration record.

subject: 110 completed trials without retrievable results
detail: 97 of them past the reporting window. Largest single addition available to this record. Not evidence of promise.
phase6_detail: For each of the 110 completed trials with no retrievable results, PubMed was searched on the registry identifier. Only 7 returned any indexed publication, and none reported the missing primary clinical outcome: PRECISIONS (design paper), one pre-completion report, one methodological paper, and four safety, pharmacokinetic or preclinical papers. Two entities were added to the landscape from these (SRN001, PMID 42052104; TNIK inhibitor, PMID 38459338), both phase 1 only. Register ipf_phase6_missing_results_retrieval.csv; map row M5.15; correction C38. The deficit is genuine non-reporting, not a search failure.

subject: Chinese-language databases
detail: CNKI, VIP, Wanfang and SinoMed were not searchable from this environment; the traditional-medicine screen therefore rests on English-indexed records only.
phase6_outcome: partially completed - direct database access blocked
phase6_detail: ChiCTR and the WHO ICTRP portal were both requested and granted at the network level. ICTRP returns 403 from its own gateway for non-browser clients, and the ChiCTR search interface requires an encrypted, bot-protected browser session; neither was circumvented. CNKI, Wanfang, VIP and SinoMed remain inaccessible and are subscription-gated. What was executed instead: English-indexed systematic reviews that had searched those databases were used to quantify the missing literature - at least 63 randomised trials of Chinese medicine injections and several further pools totalling thousands of participants, with no injection product present in the landscape (correction C35, register ipf_phase6_chinese_language_coverage.csv, map row M5.14). This measures the size of the gap; it does not close it and assigns no verdict.

subject: co-trimoxazole adherence
detail: Adherence-stratified re-analysis of EME-TIPAC, acknowledging confounding by health status in open-label per-protocol comparisons.
phase6_outcome: not executable within this record - individual participant data required
phase6_detail: EME-TIPAC (PMID 33289822) is a double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 342 patients across 39 UK centres; 283 of 342 (83%) completed, and the primary endpoint hazard ratio was 1.2 (95% CI 0.9-1.6). No adherence-stratified or per-protocol re-analysis is published, and none of the trial's 15 secondary outcomes addresses adherence. The independent CleanUP-IPF trial (PMID 33974018) is also null, with an adjusted HR of 1.15 (95% CI 0.68-1.95) in its co-trimoxazole stratum. An adherence-stratified analysis cannot be done from published summaries: it requires individual participant dosing records. Smallest next step: request the EME-TIPAC dataset from the trial team and run a prespecified analysis using instrumental-variable or inverse-probability-weighted per-protocol methods, since a naive per-protocol comparison in an open-adherence setting is confounded by health status. Priority is low: two independent randomised trials are null, so the analysis would be testing whether a null was caused by non-adherence, not testing a positive signal.

subject: corticosteroid harm magnitude
detail: Quantify mortality association in existing cohorts with explicit handling of confounding by indication.
phase6_outcome: completed - answered by existing synthesis; no new pooling warranted
phase6_detail: The question is answered as far as existing data allow, and the answer is that the magnitude is not established. A 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis (10 observational studies, 1639 patients with fibrotic ILD) found an uncertain effect of corticosteroids on mortality (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.85-1.25) and, in IPF specifically, an uncertain effect on FVC decline (mean difference -3.80% predicted, 95% CI -8.94 to 1.34), both very low certainty (PMID 38160015). In acute exacerbation the cohorts disagree in an interpretable way: no association with in-hospital mortality but worse overall survival in one propensity-weighted cohort (PMID 31846126), no advantage for pulse over non-pulse dosing (PMID 38087838), and better survival with early dose tapering (PMID 36289512). Re-pooling the same 10 observational studies would reproduce an existing analysis, so no new meta-analysis was performed. Map row M3.18. Smallest next step: a target-trial emulation in a prospective registry with time-varying corticosteroid exposure and explicit handling of confounding by indication, which requires registry data access rather than published summaries.

subject: FVC-to-survival surrogacy
detail: Trial-level or individual-participant meta-analysis; begin with a check of whether published meta-analyses already answer it.
phase6_outcome: partially completed - the published literature answers a different question
phase6_detail: The action's own first step was executed. Two primary sources address FVC and mortality: pooled nintedanib trial data (n=2583) show that a faster rate of FVC decline and a lower current FVC each predict death over 52 weeks (HR 1.79, 95% CI 1.57-2.03 and HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.17-1.32 per 5-percentage-point decrease; PMID 37646126), and a prospective registry shows adjusted 1.8-, 2.3- and 2.7-fold increases in death or transplantation after declines of at least 2%, 5% and 10% predicted (PMID 40020995). Both are patient-level prognostic analyses. Neither addresses treatment-effect surrogacy - whether a drug's effect on FVC predicts its effect on survival - which is the question this record depends on. That analysis was not attempted here: it requires paired FVC and mortality treatment effects extracted and verified trial by trial from primary reports, and individual IPF trials are underpowered for mortality. Map row M5.16. Smallest next step: assemble the trial-level dataset from primary publications and registry postings, then seek pooled individual participant data from sponsors before any surrogacy claim is made or relied upon.

subject: recovery and reversal endpoints
detail: No endpoint in the record measures recovery of lost lung function or reversal of established fibrosis.
phase6_outcome: completed - endpoint set specified, none validated
phase6_detail: Five candidate endpoints were specified for the dimensions the record cannot currently measure (reversal of established fibrosis, recovery of lost lung function, gas-transfer recovery, durable benefit after an exacerbation, and anchored functional recovery), each with a measurement approach, the existing validation evidence, feasibility, and the smallest validation step. Every one of the five smallest steps is a re-analysis of existing images or datasets, not a new trial. Register ipf_phase6_recovery_endpoints.csv. None of these endpoints is validated, and specifying them does not create evidence that recovery or reversal is achievable in IPF.

subject: STRIVE-IPF (NCT03286556) analysis and publication
detail: The largest single positive randomised signal in the record - six-month survival 44% versus 7% after acute exacerbation - exists only as a registry posting with no statistical analysis, no baseline severity data and no results paper (only design paper PMID 38509495). Smallest next step: request from the sponsor and investigators the statistical analysis plan, the baseline lung-function and oxygen-requirement table, the CONSORT flow reconciling 82 enrolled with 33 versus 18 analysed, and the primary survival analysis.
